## Unparented

### The default check does not validate the artifact the whole ledger exists to produce

`proposed` · `@akr.work.default-check-does-not-validate-the-views/1`

`akr check` reports "no diagnostics" on a workspace whose docs/generated views do not match its
ledger. View currency is only checked behind `--views-current`. A survey on 2026-09-08 of the
fifteen workspaces under /mnt/Samsung980_1TB/Rust-projects found that ten of them were shipping
views that did not match, from two distinct causes, and that plain `akr check` was clean on
every single one.

THE MEASUREMENT.

Stale by tool version, nine workspaces: akr 0.3.3 in Evidence-intake-project, orderflower,
openarc and agent-pack; akr 0.4.0 in raw-autotune, Lege-ecosystem, Thai-alphabet-app and — this
repository. pixelkit had no views at all and raised six AKR-E012. Each of the others raised
seven AKR-E011 whose only differing line was line 3, the tool version.

Stale by source-graph hash, one workspace: Kitchen-Concept was already on 0.5.0, but an agent
added two papercuts and a work record on 2026-09-04 and never ran `akr build`, so all seven
views carried the pre-addition graph. Diffing a view before and after building confirmed the
only changed line was line 2, the hash.

Already current: bpg-rs, jpegXL-rs, LegeOS, FreeCAD, SaveYourSkin.

WHY THE SECOND CAUSE IS THE ARGUMENT. Version drift is a migration artifact: it disappears once
every workspace has been rebuilt on one binary, and it will not come back until the next
release. Hash drift is not. It is an agent finishing a session without a final `akr build`,
which is the ordinary end of an ordinary session, and it will recur forever. Both are invisible
to the default check and both are caught by the flag nobody passes.

There is an earlier instance worth keeping as provenance. A bpg-rs papercut from the 0.1.0 era
records five view renderers that did not exist yet, and `akr build` and `akr check
--views-current` treating the missing views as vacuously current rather than warning. That is
the same bug in its first form: the emitter does not notice what it failed to emit.

THE ARGUMENT, PLAINLY. AKR's value proposition is that docs/generated is a faithful projection
of the ledger — it is the artifact humans and agents actually read, and the one thing a reader
cannot verify by inspection. Today "akr check: no diagnostics" is compatible with those files
being absent, rendered by a two-versions-old binary, or three records behind. The check that CI
runs does not check the output.

WHAT THE NEXT SESSION MUST DECIDE, because this is a policy call and not a patch:

(a) Make view currency part of stage F of the default check, so AKR-E011 and AKR-E012 are
ordinary diagnostics. Cost: every workspace that has not rebuilt since its last write starts
failing, which is exactly the ten found above, and that is either the point or an unacceptable
migration, depending on whether `akr build` is considered cheap. It is: a full build of the
largest ledger in the survey took 2.2 seconds.

(b) Warn rather than error when the views' tool line does not match the running binary, and
error only on the hash. This separates the migration artifact from the recurring defect and
makes only the second one block. It is the smaller change and it fixes the cause that recurs.

(c) Have `akr build` be implied by a write, so hash drift cannot happen. Rejected here without
prejudice: writes are frequent and a build is not free at every write, and D-032 deliberately
keeps the commit and the ledger write separate.

Whichever is taken, `akr check`'s summary line should say when it last saw the views agree,
rather than being silent about a thing it did not look at.

### akr import writes 125 live work items and never mentions akr ingest

`proposed` · `@akr.work.import-drafts-land-as-live-work/1`

Importing five discursive planning documents into the Lege-ecosystem ledger in 2026-08 produced
125 live `proposed` work records and a 1291-line ACTIVE-WORK.md that no one could read. Clearing
it on 2026-09-08 took 125 separate `akr abandon` calls. The records were not wrong so much as
not work: "Executive verdict", "Wall times (median of 5 runs)", "Peak RSS, single representative
run", "Reproduce", "Audit limitations", "1. Objective", "6. Quick reference", and negative
guidance like "Do not start with" and "Two traps — do NOT fix these by loosening a check".

THE MECHANISM, read in the source rather than inferred from the output.
`import::extract_markdown` emits one claim per heading, unconditionally, skipping only an empty
title and a body-less level-1 heading when other headings exist. `import::classify` is five
keyword rules and a catch-all, and the catch-all is `work`. Its own comment gives the rationale:
"everything else is `work` — the state a durable claim of unknown kind is safest in, because a
`proposed` work record asserts nothing normative." That is true about normativity and false
about the work queue. A proposed work record is rendered into ACTIVE-WORK.md and reads as a live
commitment; safety from asserting a norm is not safety from filling the backlog.

TWO THINGS THIS RECORD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM, because both were checked and are false.
First, the importer does not mis-attach body text: the excerpt is the section body's first
paragraph, taken verbatim by slicing, and the case that looked wrong is faithful — "## 3. Add
`Jp2DecodeStats`" genuinely opens with "Do not start by optimizing `MqDecoder`...". A discursive
document's first paragraph is simply a poor summary of its own heading, and the module's tests
correctly pin verbatim slicing. Second, the importer is not the source of the mis-shaped watch
globs seen in bulk-ported ledgers: neither `watches` nor `scope` appears anywhere in
import/ or ingest/.

THE SHARP PART. AKR already ships the review gate this needed, and `import` does not mention it.
`akr ingest` is preview, start, show, `mark <candidate> <disposition>`, apply, close — a
per-candidate review workflow. Nothing in `akr import --help` names it, distinguishes which
document shape each is for, or warns what a discursive document will produce. The Lege-ecosystem
port did not hit a missing feature; it used the wrong one of two, with no signpost.

THREE CANDIDATE ANSWERS, in increasing order of what they repair:

(a) `akr import --help` and docs/12-migration.md name `ingest` and say which document shape each
is for. One paragraph, fixes the next port only.

(b) `import` warns, or refuses without an explicit flag, above a threshold of drafted claims,
naming `ingest`. Small, and the threshold is a judgement to make rather than a number to guess:
the five documents here drafted between 7 and 61 claims each.

(c) The one that repairs the ledgers already in the ground: ACTIVE-WORK excludes a `proposed`
work record whose only source is `kind legacy` and which has never been revised. That is an
undispositioned import draft, not live work. It is a view-level predicate needing no schema
change, and every one of the 125 would have been invisible until someone actually adopted it —
which is exactly what `import`'s tracking record (D-022) already asks a reviewer to do.

(c) is the recommendation. It also composes with (a): once drafts are not live, `import` becomes
a reasonable default again and `ingest` is the path for a document you want to disposition
interactively.

### There is no way to orient on finished work, which is the most ordinary way work continues

`proposed` · `@akr.work.no-orientation-target-for-finished-work/1`

`akr context` refuses the two things a continuing agent actually has.

`akr context --goal <a decision>` answers AKR-X003: "a bundle anchors on a milestone, work or
track record". `akr context --goal <a completed work record>` answers AKR-X002: "is in terminal
state completed", with the help "use `akr start <task>` to find live work". And `akr start`
searches live work only. Both verified on this ledger at 0dd6057a.

So the supported path for the most ordinary continuation there is — someone finishes a
milestone, someone else builds on it — is no path at all. The agent has the completed record in
hand and cannot anchor on it; it has the decisions that govern the area and cannot anchor on
those either; and the one command it is told to fall back to is defined to exclude what it was
given. Two papercuts in the bpg-rs ledger hit this from opposite sides and neither reads like a
clean bug report, which is the tell: each author was describing one face of a hole neither could
see the shape of.

WHAT THE NEXT SESSION MUST DECIDE, and it is not "allow more kinds". A bundle anchored on
finished work is a different shape from one anchored on live work. For live work the question is
what remains and what constrains it, so the bundle leans on acceptance, blockers and open
questions. For finished work the question is what it decided and what now rests on it — the
decisions it produced, the evidence that closed it, the records that depend on it, and what has
gone stale underneath it since. Widening the kind check without answering that would return a
bundle shaped for a question nobody asked.

A decision as a goal is the same question again from the other end: a decision is not a plan, so
"context for a decision" means the records it governs and the work that implements it, which is
a neighbourhood query rather than a plan bundle. It may be that `akr impact` already answers
most of it and the honest fix is for AKR-X003 to say so, rather than for `context` to grow a
second mode.

Until this is settled the workaround is what both bpg-rs agents ended up doing: `akr get` on the
named records and `akr search` for the neighbourhood. That works and it is not discoverable, and
the error messages should say it — AKR-X002's help currently points at `akr start`, which is
guaranteed not to find what the reader is holding.

### 510 provenance edges mean whatever their target says now

`proposed` · `@akr.work.provenance-edges-that-follow-their-target/1`

A scan of fifteen workspaces on 2026-09-08 found 510 unversioned `derived_from` edges across
twelve of them, alongside nine unversioned `supersedes` and one unversioned `contradicts`.

`derived_from` is one of the three historical relations (Relation::is_historical, "the three
historical relations exist to point backwards"), and D-009 4.1 case 1 states the rule outright:
provenance pins, because a record was "derived from that observation, not from whatever
replaces it". An unversioned reference resolves to whichever revision is live at build time. So
every one of those 510 edges currently means "derived from whatever that record says now" — and
silently changes meaning each time its target is revised, without anyone editing the record that
claims the provenance.

This is the same defect D-044 refused for `supersedes`, at fifty times the scale, and it is
worse in kind. A re-aimed `supersedes` makes a false claim about the graph, which a reader can
at least see is odd; a re-aimed `derived_from` quietly relabels where a conclusion came from,
which is the one thing a provenance edge exists to be trusted about.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF D-044. Nine edges is a mechanical migration and was done in the same pass.
510, spread over twelve ledgers this session does not own, is a project: each edge has to be
pinned to the revision the author actually derived from, and that revision is frequently not
the current head — which means reading each one rather than rewriting them in bulk. Extending
D-044's refusal to `derived_from` today would have failed twelve workspaces at once with no
migration path, and the pressure to get them green again would have produced exactly the bulk
rewrite that destroys the information the pin is supposed to carry.

WHAT THE NEXT SESSION MUST DECIDE, in order.
First, whether a bulk pin-to-current-head is acceptable for any subset. It is defensible only
where the target has exactly one revision, since there the unversioned and pinned forms already
denote the same thing and the rewrite loses nothing. That subset should be measured before
anything else, because it may be most of the 510 and it is the only part that can be automated.
Second, what to do with the remainder, where the target has been revised and the correct pin is
a judgement about what the author meant. Reading them is the honest answer and it is not cheap.
Third, whether the refusal then extends to `derived_from` and `contradicts`, closing the class.

One measurement to take first, because it determines whether this is a day or a week: of the 510,
how many name a target that has only ever had one revision.

Drop context sections by relevance and add per-section and acceptance-only

### Give the agent scratch directory a lifecycle

`proposed` · `@akr.work.scratch-lifecycle/1`

Give `.agent/scratch/` a lifecycle, so the one disposable directory nothing empties
on its own stops growing until a person clears it by hand.

Measurement and reporting, not deletion by default: `akr check` prints what is there
as a build fact, `knowledge.start` says the same at orientation, and
`akr check --scratch-clean` is the opt-in gate. `akr scratch prune` removes unkept
entries by age and `akr scratch keep` protects one with a reason, so an agent can
tidy up at the end of a session without being able to delete what the next session
was told to expect. See D-036.
